findings.source_quote: εἶτα ἐπέδωκαν οἱ τὰ δύο μέρη χλωρὰ ἔχοντες, τὸ δὲ τρίτον ξηρόν·
findings.english_quote: Next came the people whose rods were two-thirds green and one-third dry.
findings.issue: The source explicitly says this group handed in their rods. “Next came” preserves the sequence but omits that group-level action. The subsequent descriptions of what many and others handed in do not fully translate the opening clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Then the people whose rods were two-thirds green and one-third dry handed them in.”

findings.source_quote: εἶτα ἐπέδωκαν οἱ τὰ δύο μέρη ξηρὰ ἔχοντες, τὸ δὲ τρίτον χλωρόν.
findings.english_quote: Next came the people whose rods were two-thirds dry and one-third green.
findings.issue: Within the disclosed editorial supplement, the selected working text explicitly states that this group handed in their rods. “Next came” omits that action from the opening clause. Its supplemented status does not remove the need to translate it faithfully when retaining this working reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Then the people whose rods were two-thirds dry and one-third green handed them in.” Retain the existing disclosure of the paragraph’s supplemented status and shorter alternative.

findings.source_quote: ἐπέδωκαν δὲ οἱ τὰς ῥάβδους αὐτῶν χλωρὰς ἐσχηκότες, ἐλάχιστον δὲ [ξηρὸν] καὶ σχισμὰς ἐχούσας.
findings.english_quote: Next came the people whose rods had been green, with a very small dry part and cracks.
findings.issue: The opening statement that this group handed in their rods is replaced by a sequencing expression. Although the following sentences describe subgroup submissions, they do not preserve the explicit action predicated of the group in this clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “The people whose rods had been green, with a very small dry part and cracks, also handed them in.” Retain the note identifying “dry” as supplied in the working edition.

summary: Both editions were independently checked against all six paragraphs of the selected working Greek. The standard edition preserves the clauses, group distinctions, proportions, rod conditions, and reasons for rejoicing. The simplified edition omits the opening group-level handing-in statements in paragraphs 3–5. Both editions distinguish editorial supplements from preserved text and disclose alternatives without replacing the selected working reading. This assessment uses the supplied text and bounded project reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify an exhaustive collation. Proposed revisions require fresh review.
